approach:
After each producer pass, once the replay and the in-loop checks are done and before the loop can `break Some(report)` (producer.rs:507-527), Athena runs the real-records criteria in its own process. The new `Athena::loop_records_criteria` in the new `run/records_criteria.rs` does this.

1. Select. A behavior criterion is selected when its whitespace-collapsed, lowercase text holds `status --snapshot` and `real records` (`REAL_RECORDS_PHRASES`, surveys.rs:416). Its command is the first backticked span that holds `status --snapshot`, in any form (`cargo run -p athena-cli -- status --snapshot evidence`, `athena status --snapshot evidence`, or a bare `status --snapshot evidence`). The token after `--snapshot` (a word, or `<evidence directory>` through its closing `>`) is replaced by the job's evidence directory (`crate::snapshot::evidence_dir`, mod.rs:1153) and trailing arguments are kept. Every selected command runs as `cargo run -p athena-cli -- status --snapshot <evidence> [rest]`, so it measures the producer's tree.
2. Package gate (finding 4). The mapped command needs the `athena-cli` package. `athena_cli_package(work_tree)` is true only when `<work tree>/crates/athena-cli/Cargo.toml` is a file holding a line `name = "athena-cli"` (the same file-test style as `is_athena_source`, mirrors.rs:941; the real file has `name = "athena-cli"` at line 2). The gate reads the producer's work tree (`snapshot.dir()`), so it is true for Athena's own source, the only place the gate's measure paths exist (surveys.rs:410-413). Elsewhere every selected criterion is recorded as `not run: this repository has no athena-cli package, so the command cannot run here`, with no reach check, no run and no send-back. The module docs state this.
3. Reach, once per pass, after the package gate and before running. Athena's own read (`is_dir`, `crate::snapshot::read_history`), then the producer's permission: `reach(evidence, &Policy)` calls `athena_agent::policy::evaluate(&policy, "Read", {file_path: <evidence>/history.json}, None)` on the policy file the pass ran under (`spec.hook.policy_file`, written by `agent_spec`, reading.rs:415-425). Either failure ends the job through `self.failure` with `Flow::Stop` and no verifier. The reason is in the stored form of step 6.
4. Run. Use `SnapExec { in_loop: true }`, `ExposedIndex` and `Exec::exec` in the producer's work tree (checks.rs:73-162, 283-317, 375-457). The `CheckSpec` has kind `CheckKind::Command` (success is exit 0), `skip_when_only: None`, name `records-criterion-<n>`. The command is wrapped as `sh -c '"$@" > "$0"' <job_dir>/records-criterion-<n>.out <argv>`, so Athena reads the command's whole stdout from a file it owns; cargo's stderr is kept only as an error tail. A non-zero exit, a timeout, low disk, a busy slot or any error becomes a `not run` entry with its reason and is never sent back. Only the kill switch and an unreachable snapshot stop the job.
5. Judge, by rules written in the module docs (revised for findings 1 and 2).
   - Judged lines: stdout lines that hold the measure phrase (the words after `real records` between `the` and `it prints` / `it shows` / `is within`). No phrase, or no judged line, is `not judged` with the reason.
   - The head of a judged line is the text after the first occurrence of the phrase, cut at the first `;` or `(`. Figures after a `;`, inside parentheses, or on later occurrences are never judged.
   - The figure is the FIRST number in the head directly followed by a unit of the range's family (alias table: minutes = min, mins, minute, minutes; seconds = s, sec, secs, second, seconds; hours = h, hr, hrs, hour, hours; usd = usd, or a `$` before the number; percent = %, percent; no conversion between families). A word such as `landing(s)` or `check(s)` is not a unit (whole-word match). No figure in the head is `not judged`.
   - The range is `<lo> to|and|- <hi> <unit>` after `expected range`. A figure outside it is a problem. No parsable range means the figure is shown, not judged.
   - Constant: only a per-item list counts. It is the first parenthesised group on a judged line after the phrase whose entries, split on ` · `, are ALL `<job id> <number>[ unit]`, with job id `\d{8}-\d{6}-\w{4}`, and with at least three entries. It is a problem when every entry holds the same number. A list with any non-job-id label (stage names, dates) is never a per-item list, whatever the criterion says. There is no per-item-wording branch. A constant needs no stated range.
6. Stored form (the machine-path rule). Everything stored carries no machine path: `brief-verifier.md`, the invocation `detail` and the job's failure reason. The run's command, output, judged lines and error tail pass through the redactor and then the state root is replaced by `<state>`. The real evidence path becomes `evidence_placeholder(id)`. Problem text names the criterion number, the figure and the range, never the command or a path. Text sent to an agent (the producer send-back and the sent verifier brief) has the placeholder replaced by the real evidence path, as the evidence section does (mod.rs:1155-1158; verification.rs:179-214 builds the brief once with the placeholder and once with the real path).
7. Verdict (choice b, named in D183). Athena's run is not a CheckRun, so `verify::judge` does not count it as seen running (verify.rs:411-445, 573-603). The verifier entry says it is Athena's run, does not count as the verifier's command, and that the verifier must run the same command in its snapshot and cite it.
8. Hand-off. Problems join the one shared send-back (`problems`, `report_problems`, `PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS`); at the limit they reach the verifier as `producer-report-gaps`. Every run, judged or not, reaches the verifier: `Reported` and `Built` carry `records_runs`, and `verification_stage` pushes one `CheckResultView` per run (`records-criterion-<n>`, command `not a check`) with a new `records_run: Option<RecordsRunView>`. No record kind is added, so `check_record_file`, `AnyRecord` and `ResumeMark` are unchanged.

Known limit, stated in the module docs, D183, the CHANGELOG and the open question (finding 3): today's `status --snapshot` prints only medians and totals (throughput.rs:836-844), with no per-job list labelled by job ids, so on current output the constant rule cannot fire. It fires when the producer's change makes the command print such a list, which a change to a per-job measure does. The range rule fires today for any criterion that states a numeric range and whose phrase names a line that prints a figure in that unit. A candidate taken through the resume shortcut (mod.rs:818-828, no producer pass) gets no records run; a retry that runs the producer again gets one after each pass.

Tests are pure unit tests in records_criteria.rs and fake-producer tests named `records_loop_*` in run/tests.rs. The seam is a thread-local `argv_seam` that mirrors `demo_seam` (checks.rs:585-615) and maps only the inner `cargo run` argv. The redirect, the reading of stdout, the package gate, the judging, the stored form and the send-back are production code. Fake-producer tests commit `crates/athena-cli/Cargo.toml` into the test repository with the existing `commit_file` (tests.rs:358), so the package gate runs for real.

decisions.choice: Finding 1: judge only the first figure in the range's unit family in the head of a judged line (text after the phrase, cut at the first `;` or `(`). Figures after a `;`, inside parentheses or after the head are ignored.
decisions.reason: The real lines print comparison figures in the same unit. throughput.rs:794 appends `; the {n} landings before: {figure}` to the USD and percent lines (798-805): `spent on attempts that did not land: 1.23 USD over the last 5 landing(s); the 5 landings before: 0.40 USD` and `landed on the first attempt: 60% over the last 5 landing(s); the 5 landings before: 20%`. The build-wait line is `build wait {total} s over {n} check(s), longest {longest} s` (832-833). Taking every unit-matching figure would judge 0.40 USD, 20% or the longest wait against the range and spend the one shared send-back on correct work. The first figure after the phrase is the current value on all three; `median per landed job over the last 3 measured: 4.0 min (stages)` and `did not land: 2 job(s), 3.4 min` also give their figure first (`3 measured` and `2 job(s)` have no unit). Unit tests use literal lines copied from throughput.rs:794-805, 810, 832 and 837, assert that only the current figure is judged, and the real-text test runs `Throughput::text()` for the lines a job produces.

rejected.option: Judge every figure on the line that is in the range's unit family
rejected.why: Judges the `landings before` comparison and `longest` figures, so correct work is sent back (the critic's false positive).

rejected.option: Judge the first number on each line
rejected.why: Hits history counts, hash digits, `3 measured` and `2 job(s)`.

rejected.option: Use run_check's `output_tail` as the judged output
rejected.why: It is the last 4096 bytes of stdout and stderr merged, so item lines could be cut and cargo `--> file:line:col` lines parsed; Athena reads the whole stdout from a file it owns instead.

rejected.option: Import RECORDS_MEASURE_PHRASES from reading/surveys.rs
rejected.why: It is `pub(super)` in the gate module, which is out of scope, and a list cannot name a measure the producer adds.

rejected.option: Run `status --snapshot --json` and read a named field
rejected.why: No map from a phrase such as `landing time` to a JSON field exists, and the recorded command would differ from the criterion's.

decisions.choice: Finding 2: a per-item list is only a parenthesised ` · ` list whose labels ALL are job ids (`\d{8}-\d{6}-\w{4}`), with at least three entries. Constant means every entry holds the same number. The per-item-wording branch is dropped.
decisions.reason: `StageMinutes::named()` returns six stages (reading, planning, producer, checks, verifier, landing and rebuild; throughput.rs:113-121) printed as `({name} {m:.1} · ...)` (806-812), and planning, checks and landing are often all 0.0. With a wording branch a criterion saying `per job` whose phrase matches the median line would flag equal stage medians as constant. With job-id labels only, stage names and `{day} {landed}` daily counts (813-818) are never per-item lists whatever the criterion says, so the unit test `equal stage medians with per-item wording give no problem` is satisfied by the rule and not by luck. `Constant` is every entry equal, at least three entries; two equal entries, or three with one different, are not constant. This is the request's `same answer for every item`. The gate's own failing example, a landing time of 0.1 minutes for every job (surveys.rs:591), is a per-job list.

rejected.option: Accept lists of non-date labels when the criterion says per job / each job / every item
rejected.why: Matches the stage-median list, so equal stage medians would be called constant; the rule could not pass its own test.

rejected.option: Two or more equal items of any `label number` list
rejected.why: Equal daily landed counts and equal stage medians are common and are not per-item values.

rejected.option: Never judge constants, only the range
rejected.why: The request names the constant measure as a send-back reason, and the gate's usual criterion states no number.

decisions.choice: Finding 3: state the limit in the module docs, D183, the CHANGELOG, the producer-brief sentence and the open question: a constant can be caught only when the command prints a per-job list labelled by job ids, which today's `status --snapshot` does not print; the range check needs a numeric range in the criterion and a judged line with a figure in its unit.
decisions.reason: throughput.rs:836-844 prints `throughput N landed (days)`, a median with stage medians, idle, unlanded and waste lines, and build wait. `landed_jobs` (throughput.rs:472) holds per-job stage minutes, but `text()` prints none of them. Demonstrations 1-3 therefore use a printed per-job line the seam supplies, which stands for what a change to a per-job measure would print. Athena computing per-item values itself would be a new computation the code does not define, so it is asked as a question, not planned.

rejected.option: Compute per-job values from the snapshot inside Athena
rejected.why: A new measure computation the code does not define, and it would run a different calculation from the command the verifier is told to run; asked as a question instead.

rejected.option: Change `status --snapshot` to print per-job values
rejected.why: A user-facing output change made only for Athena's check; out of scope and the producer brief says not to do it.

decisions.choice: Finding 4: gate the stage on the repository. `athena_cli_package(work_tree)` (a real file test in every build) must hold, else each selected criterion is a `not run` entry naming the missing package, with no reach check, no run and no send-back.
decisions.reason: Selection matches only the text `status --snapshot` and `real records`, but the mapped command `cargo run -p athena-cli` exists only where that package does. The measure paths the reading gate watches are Athena's own files (surveys.rs:410-413), so in practice the package is there. The gate is a file test on the producer's work tree (`snapshot.dir()`), which has `crates/athena-cli/Cargo.toml` with `name = "athena-cli"` in Athena's source (line 2) and none elsewhere. Tests commit the file with `commit_file` (tests.rs:358) so the real check runs; a second test omits it and asserts the entry and a zero seam count; unit tests cover a tree with the package, without it, and with another package name.

rejected.option: Gate on the change touching RECORDS_MEASURE_PATHS
rejected.why: Those paths are `pub(super)` in the gate module (out of scope), and a status measure may live in a file the list lacks; the package test asks the question that matters, whether the command can run.

rejected.option: Test-build shortcut where an installed seam counts as the package
rejected.why: Puts the logic under test in the double and leaves the gate untested end to end.

rejected.option: Reuse `is_athena_source` (mirrors.rs:941)
rejected.why: It also needs `setup.sh` and the timings file, which say nothing about whether `cargo run -p athena-cli` works.

decisions.choice: Everything stored holds the placeholder form: command, output, judged lines, error tail, problem text, the unreachable failure reason. Only text sent to an agent has the placeholder replaced by the real evidence path.
decisions.reason: mod.rs:1155-1156 keeps machine paths out of stored briefs, and verification.rs:179-191 stores `brief-verifier.md` built from the same `inputs`. The first stdout line of the command is `snapshot    {dir}` (display.rs:1198), the absolute path, so raw output would break the rule. The invocation `detail` (producer.rs:590-594) joins the problem text, so that text never holds a command or a path. `self.failure` stores its reason, so the unreachable reason names `<state>/jobs/<id>/evidence`. The briefs renderer replaces `evidence_placeholder(job)` by the `evidence` argument it is given, so the stored call and the sent call differ only there.

rejected.option: Store the real path in `RecordsRunView`
rejected.why: Breaks the stored-brief rule.

rejected.option: Strip the output line that holds the path
rejected.why: Hides data the verifier may need; the state-root replacement keeps every line.

decisions.choice: Verdict choice (b): the verifier entry says it is Athena's own run, does not count as the verifier's command, and must be run again in the verifier's snapshot and cited. verify.rs, records.rs and CheckRun are unchanged.
decisions.reason: `verify::judge` builds `ran` from the verifier's `commands_run` and passing CheckRuns (verify.rs:411-445) and marks a behavior criterion unmet when its cited command was not seen running (573-603). Counting Athena's run (choice a) needs a new CheckRun field or a verify.rs rule, and neither file is a deliverable. `revert_for` (records.rs:893-901) means a run with the fix reverted, so reusing it would misdescribe the run. With (b) the failure the request names (evidence that cites no command that ran) is fixed from the verifier side: the verifier sees the command and Athena's figures, runs the same command and cites it. Tests: a fake verifier that runs and cites the command reaches Landed; one that cites it without running it is unmet with the D43 finding.

rejected.option: (a) Make Athena's run count as seen running
rejected.why: Needs a record or verify.rs change outside the deliverables and would let a verifier cite a run it never repeated.

rejected.option: Reuse `revert_for` on a stored CheckRun
rejected.why: Its documented meaning is a run with the fix reverted; this run is on the unreverted tree.

decisions.choice: Any selected `status --snapshot <token>` command, whatever its prefix, runs as `cargo run -p athena-cli -- status --snapshot <evidence>` plus trailing arguments; the shown command is that string in stored form.
decisions.reason: reading.rs:8552-8584 tests accept `Run `status --snapshot evidence`: on the real records ...`, so the gate accepts bare and `athena` forms. An installed `athena status` would print the old measure; `cargo run` measures the producer's tree and matches the command the evidence section tells the verifier to run (briefs.rs:671). Unit tests cover the bare, `athena`, `cargo run` and wrapped-line forms, the `evidence` token and `<evidence directory>`.

rejected.option: Skip a command that is not `cargo run` with a `not run` entry
rejected.why: Silently drops criteria the gate accepts, which is the failure the request is about.

rejected.option: Run `self.athena_bin status --snapshot <dir>`
rejected.why: That is the installed Athena, not the producer's change.

decisions.choice: The wrapper `CheckSpec` has kind `CheckKind::Command`, `skip_when_only: None`, name `records-criterion-<n>`, run `sh -c ...`, through the in-loop `SnapExec`.
decisions.reason: run_check rewrites cargo test args for `CheckKind::Test` (checks.rs:526-530) and fails a test check that ran zero tests (594-598); `Command` is the default kind where success is exit 0 (config.rs:474-480). `isolate`, `kill_group` and the poll loop are private to checks.rs, so reusing `Exec::exec` avoids a copy that would need to be kept in step. The in-loop `SnapExec` reads no check seam (checks.rs:131-134), so the records seam is separate.

rejected.option: CheckKind::Test
rejected.why: Fails the run for running zero tests.

rejected.option: A second process runner in records_criteria.rs
rejected.why: Copies private code.

decisions.choice: Keep the producer-permission half of `reach` and state its limit in D183: it catches only a policy built while the folder was missing (`agent_spec` writes `evidence` only when `dir.is_dir()` at spawn, reading.rs:415-416; athena-agent has no OS sandbox). It calls `evaluate(..., None)` with an absolute file path. `reach` is tested directly with `Policy` values, not through a forged policy file.
decisions.reason: The reading defines unreachable as missing or not readable by the producer's grant. policy.rs:35-47 documents `evidence` as a directory outside the snapshot that may be read, never written; `evaluate` has the signature `evaluate(policy, tool, input, cwd: Option<&Path>)` (policy.rs:90). The end-to-end early end is shown by the removed-directory test.

rejected.option: Drop the policy half
rejected.why: The reading names the grant case.

rejected.option: Check only before the first pass
rejected.why: The policy is built from the same `is_dir()` test dispatch just satisfied (mod.rs:1153-1154), so a first-pass check never fires in a real job.

decisions.choice: The producer-brief sentence describes how Athena judges and asks for no output change: 'Athena also runs each behavior criterion that names real records and gives a `status --snapshot` command, on your work tree, and records the command and its output for the verifier. It sends you back only when a line that holds the criterion's phrase prints a figure outside the stated range, or a parenthesised list of three or more job ids that all show the same value; other output is only recorded. Do not change what a command prints to satisfy this check.' A briefs test asserts the sentence and that it holds no request to reformat output.
decisions.reason: A sentence that asked producers to print a phrase would invite user-facing `status` changes made only for Athena's check.

rejected.option: Tell the producer to print the measure on a line that holds the criterion's phrase
rejected.why: Invites output changes that exist only to satisfy the check.

decisions.choice: Send back only a constant per-job list or a figure outside the stated range; record everything else (non-zero exit, timeout, skip, no package, unidentifiable measure, no figure) as `not run` or `not judged`, with its reason, for the verifier. Send-backs reuse `PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS`.
decisions.reason: The request names two send-back reasons. A build failure in the producer's tree is already a failing in-loop check (checks.rs:447-455), so a second send-back would report it twice and spend the shared send-back on an environment error.

rejected.option: Send back a non-zero exit
rejected.why: Duplicates the in-loop check and adds a reason the request did not ask for.

decisions.choice: Hold the evidence in `Reported` and `Built` as `records_runs: Vec<RecordsRun>`, shown as `CheckResultView` entries with a new optional `records_run: Option<RecordsRunView>`, rendered by a dedicated briefs function. `ResumeMark` is unchanged. crates/athena-agent/src/fake.rs is not modified and is named under `unchanged_planned_files` with this reason.
decisions.reason: This follows the `producer-report-gaps` and `ci-result` entries (verification.rs:88-127). The existing `demonstration` field renders `fails without the fix ... fix reverted` text (briefs.rs:989-1036), and `failed_check_detail` shows no output for a passed entry (briefs.rs:1062-1063), so a dedicated field and renderer are needed. The `Script` closure already receives the whole `AgentInvocation` and `FakeTurn` has `edits` and `commands_run` (fake.rs:16-21, 43, 97-111), so the fixtures (fix on send-back, remove the evidence directory, a verifier that cites a command it ran) are scripts in tests.rs.

rejected.option: A records field on `ResumeMark`
rejected.why: state.rs is not a deliverable; the resume shortcut runs no producer pass.

rejected.option: A new record kind or file under records/
rejected.why: The request keeps the output as check evidence in the existing form.

rejected.option: A records-aware fake turn in fake.rs
rejected.why: Test-only structure for behavior a closure already expresses.

decisions.choice: Test reading: keep the base test reading (capability `study`, class `docs`, tests.rs:227-231) and add or swap a `"kind": "behavior"` criterion, as tests.rs:1368 does. Add no refusal-corpus case.
decisions.reason: `check_code_survey` and `check_records_measure` apply only to class `code` or `tests` (surveys.rs:237-241), so the docs reading is accepted and admission's demonstration rules apply only in planning, which `repo()` leaves off. The new selection, phrase, range, list and package parsers consume readings the gate accepted and refuse nothing; `refusal_corpus` runs reading checks, never the run stage. Input forms the parsers handle and the corpus cases that hold them (read at refusal_corpus.rs:427, 436, 452): backticked `cargo run -p athena-cli -- status --snapshot evidence` with `real records` and a range with no number is `records-measure-change-with-real-records-range-history-json` and `...-range-git-log`; the wrapped line is `refusal-rate-declaration-wrapped-line`; the bare and `athena` command forms are tested at reading.rs:8552-8584, not in the corpus. The `<evidence directory>` token, each numeric range form (`2 to 10 minutes`, `between 2 and 10`, `2-10`), no range, the unit aliases and the list forms have no corpus case and no corpus case is added, because they are unit-tested in records_criteria.rs and are not refusals. The corpus test is still run as a demonstration (criterion 7).

rejected.option: Class `code` with a Code survey assumption
rejected.why: Brings the reading gates into a run-stage test for no benefit.

rejected.option: New corpus cases for the numeric-range forms
rejected.why: The corpus tests refusal outcomes; refusal_corpus.rs is not a deliverable and the new code is not on that path.

decisions.choice: Append D183 to docs/decisions.md after D182 with a Provenance bullet naming D182 (the in-loop checks), D115 and D156 as standing. It records the verdict choice (b), the stored-form rule, what is judged (first figure in the head; job-id lists only), what is only recorded, the no-per-job-list limit on current output, the package gate, the reach limit and the resume-shortcut limit.
decisions.reason: A new stage and send-back rule before the verifier is a decision later jobs will cite. Nothing existing is edited. docs/decision-links.toml:220-224 governs only candidate.rs and athena-git snapshot.rs, which this plan does not touch.

rejected.option: No decision entry
rejected.why: docs/decisions.md is a listed deliverable and the rule changes when a job can end.

files.purpose: The pre-verifier records run. `RecordsRun`, `RecordsVerdict`; `select` and command mapping (any `status --snapshot <token>` span mapped to `cargo run -p athena-cli -- status --snapshot <evidence>`); `athena_cli_package(work_tree)` (finding 4); `measure_phrase`, `stated_range`, the unit alias table, `judge` (judged lines; the first figure in the range's unit family in the head cut at `;` or `(` (finding 1); per-item lists only with job-id labels, at least three entries, constant means every entry equal (finding 2)) with the rules and the no-per-job-list limit in the module docs; `reach` (Athena's read and `evaluate` on a `Policy`); `Athena::loop_records_criteria` (package gate, reach, SnapExec in_loop, ExposedIndex, `CheckKind::Command` spec, the `sh` redirect wrapper, skip lines, kill switch); the stored-form helper (state root to `<state>`); `append_records_problems`; cfg-gated `argv_seam` and `records_runs_here`; unit tests for each rule and input form.

Call `loop_records_criteria` after `loop_check_failures` and before `break Some(report)`, passing the pass's policy file. On `unreachable`, call `self.failure` (stored-form reason) and return `Flow::Stop`. Add the records problems to the break condition, `problems` and `report_problems`. Wrap `attempt_brief` with `append_records_problems` (the real evidence path in the sent text). Add `records_runs` to `Reported`. Extend the `producer_loop` doc with the root cause and limits.
Declare `mod records_criteria;`; add `records_runs` to `Built` (resume path: empty) and take it from `Reported`; update the `PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS` doc to name the records run.
Push one `CheckResultView` per `RecordsRun` (name `records-criterion-<n>`, command `not a check`, passed true, `records_run: Some(..)`, stored-form text) after the `producer-report-gaps` entry.

Add `RecordsRunView` and `CheckResultView.records_run`; a renderer in the verifier brief's checks list (command, result sentence, judged lines, clipped output as data, and the sentence that this is Athena's run and must be run and cited by the verifier) that replaces `evidence_placeholder(job)` by the `evidence` argument; one sentence in the producer brief's `## Checks before the verifier` that describes judging (figure outside the range, or a job-id list that is all equal) and asks for no output change; `records_run: None` where tests list every field; new briefs tests.

The fake-producer tests `records_loop_*` named in the demonstrations (constant, in range, lands with a citing verifier, citing-without-running unmet, out of range, unreachable, stored versus sent text, fixture-only runs nothing, no athena-cli package, busy slot, real throughput text); a helper that adds the behavior criterion to the reader, producer and verifier scripts (the `scoped` pattern); a helper that commits `crates/athena-cli/Cargo.toml` with `commit_file`; a verifier-script wrapper that sets `commands_run` and `commands`; a helper that builds the real-shaped status block; a seam installer.

risks.risk: The judge compares the wrong numbers and sends back correct work, or misses a constant measure.
risks.mitigation: Only lines that hold the criterion's own phrase are judged. Only the first figure in the range's unit family in the head (cut at `;` or `(`) counts, so `the N landings before` comparisons and `longest` figures are never judged. A list counts only with at least three job-id labels, so stage medians and daily counts never do. Stdout only is read. Anything not identified is `not judged` with its reason and sends nothing back. The rules are in the module docs and unit-tested on literal copies of the real status lines (USD, percent, build wait, median with stages, throughput with days, header, dates, hashes, cargo lines) and on a real `Throughput::text()`.

risks.risk: On current output the constant rule cannot fire, and for the gate's usual wording (no number, `the landing time it prints`) no line holds the phrase, so for many real jobs nothing is judged.
risks.mitigation: Stated in the module docs, D183, the CHANGELOG, the producer sentence and the open questions. The verifier entry shows `not judged: <reason>` with the whole output and tells the verifier to run and cite the command, so the stage still removes the cause named in the request: Athena runs the command and the verifier sees its output.

risks.risk: The verifier does not repeat the command, so the behavior criterion is still unmet at the verdict (choice b).
risks.mitigation: The entry says so in plain words next to the command, and the command is the one the evidence section already tells the verifier to run (briefs.rs:671). The end-to-end tests show a verifier that runs and cites it lands and one that cites it without running it does not. D183 names the choice.

risks.risk: A pre-verifier `cargo run` adds build time on each pass of these jobs.
risks.mitigation: It runs only for a behavior criterion that holds both `status --snapshot` and `real records`, only where the package exists, in the producer's own `target/produce`, with a slot only if one is free and within `check_timeout_s`. A busy slot, low disk or any error is a skip line and a `not run` entry, never a stop. Only the kill switch and an unreachable snapshot end the job.

risks.risk: The `sh -c '"$@" > "$0"'` wrapper fails on a host without `sh` on the check environment's PATH.
risks.mitigation: The environment is `athena_agent::env::build` for `Side::Produce`, the one the in-loop checks use for `cargo`. A missing `sh` makes the run fail to start, recorded as `not run`, and nothing is sent back. The test seam uses `sh` too.

risks.risk: The state-root replacement misses a machine path outside the state directory, or replaces too much.
risks.mitigation: The evidence, job and work-tree paths are all under the state root (the evidence path ends in `/jobs/<id>/evidence`, asserted in a unit test). The stored-versus-sent test checks the real state path appears nowhere in the stored verifier brief, invocation detail or failure reason, and that the sent prompts hold the real evidence path. A path outside the state root in a cargo error tail is clipped and quoted as data.

risks.risk: The package file test differs from what `cargo run -p athena-cli` needs (for example a renamed package, or a workspace member listed elsewhere).
risks.mitigation: A false `not run` only records the command for the verifier and sends nothing back; a false pass leads to a `not run` entry from the failed cargo call. Neither sends back or ends a job. The test is the plain file-and-name check, unit-tested with the package, without it, and with another name.

risks.risk: The Landed test needs everything else in the harness to pass.
risks.mitigation: It follows `a_failing_check_is_sent_back_before_the_verifier_and_the_fix_reaches_it` (tests.rs:4543), which lands on the same harness and the same checks; only the verifier script differs. The extra `crates/athena-cli/Cargo.toml` is committed to the base, not at the root, so the root-`Cargo.toml` tests of producer.rs:185 are not affected. If another verdict reason blocks it, the test reports `finished.reason` and the producer fixes the fixture, not the production rule.

risks.risk: The real-text test needs `Throughput::compute` to return a value for a job the fake agents landed.
risks.mitigation: crates/athena-cli/tests/status_snapshot.rs:97-100 shows a landed job has throughput in the cli fixture. If it is `None` in the core harness, the producer moves that one test to athena-cli/tests with the judge reached through a documented `pub` re-export, and reports which.

risks.risk: The thread-local `argv_seam` is not seen if a test runs the job on another thread.
risks.mitigation: The mapper is installed per test and cleared by its guard, as `demo_seam` is. `records_runs_here` mirrors `demo_runs_here`, so a build without an installed seam runs nothing. The loop tests run `Athena::go` on the test thread, as the existing demonstration tests do.
